title: Custom domain
content:
## Overview

Every web app deployed on Emergent receives a free subdomain at `yourappname.emergent.build`. To present your app under your own brand, add a custom domain through the **Deployments** panel. Custom domains require you to configure DNS records with your domain registrar (e.g., Cloudflare, Namecheap, GoDaddy) and point them to Emergent's infrastructure.

This page walks you through DNS setup, troubleshooting, and common questions about the default subdomain.

<Note>
Custom domains are available for **web apps only**. Mobile apps use their own distribution channels (App Store, Play Store) and do not rely on DNS.
</Note>

---

## DNS: A record + Emergent IP

To serve your app at your root domain (e.g., `example.com`), add an **A record** that points to the IP address shown in the custom domain configuration flow.

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the custom domain panel">
In the Emergent workspace, navigate to **Deployments** → **Custom Domain** (web apps only). Click **Add Custom Domain**.
</Step>

<Step title="Copy the Emergent IP address">
The panel displays a dedicated IP address for your app. Copy this IP — you will use it in the next step.
</Step>

<Step title="Create an A record at your DNS provider">
Log in to your domain registrar or DNS host (Cloudflare, Namecheap, etc.). Add a new **A record**:

- **Host / Name**: `@` (or leave blank, depending on your provider)
- **Type**: `A`
- **Value / Points to**: the IP address from step 2
- **TTL**: `Auto` or `3600` (1 hour)

Save the record.
</Step>

<Step title="Confirm the domain in Emergent">
Return to the custom domain panel, enter your domain (e.g., `example.com`), and click **Verify**. Emergent will check for the A record and provision an SSL certificate once the record is detected.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout type="info" title="SSL provisioning">
SSL certificates are issued automatically via Let's Encrypt after DNS verification. This usually takes a few minutes but can take up to 24 hours if DNS propagation is slow.
</Callout>

---

## CNAME (`www`) entry

Most users expect both `example.com` and `www.example.com` to work. Add a **CNAME record** to route `www` traffic to your root domain.

<Steps>
<Step title="Add the CNAME record">
In your DNS provider's dashboard, create a new **CNAME** record:

- **Host / Name**: `www`
- **Type**: `CNAME`
- **Value / Points to**: `example.com` (your root domain, no `http://`)
- **TTL**: `Auto` or `3600`

Save the record.
</Step>

<Step title="Test both URLs">
After DNS propagates, visit both `https://example.com` and `https://www.example.com`. Both should load your app. Emergent automatically redirects `www` to the root domain (or vice versa, depending on your configuration).
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip>
Some DNS providers (like Cloudflare) also support **CNAME flattening** or **ALIAS records** at the root. If you prefer to use a CNAME instead of an A record, consult your provider's documentation.
</Tip>

---

## Troubleshooting a stuck domain

If your custom domain does not load after adding DNS records, follow these checks:

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Verify DNS records are correct">
Use a DNS lookup tool (e.g., [dnschecker.org](https://dnschecker.org) or `dig example.com` in your terminal) to confirm:

- The **A record** for `@` (root) points to the Emergent IP.
- The **CNAME** for `www` points to your root domain.

If the records are missing or incorrect, update them at your DNS provider and allow a few minutes for propagation.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Wait for DNS propagation">
DNS changes can take anywhere from a few minutes to 48 hours to propagate globally, depending on your provider and the previous TTL. If you recently added or changed records, wait 1–2 hours and check again.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Check SSL certificate status">
In the Emergent **Deployments** panel, the custom domain row shows a status badge (e.g., **Pending**, **Active**, **Error**). If it says **Pending**, SSL provisioning is in progress. If it says **Error**, click **Details** to see the specific issue (often a DNS mismatch or CAA record blocking Let's Encrypt).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Clear your browser cache">
Browsers and operating systems cache DNS lookups. Try visiting your domain in an **incognito/private window** or run `ipconfig /flushdns` (Windows) / `sudo dscacheutil -flushcache` (macOS) to clear local caches.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

<Warning>
If your domain registrar uses **proxy/CDN mode** (e.g., Cloudflare's orange cloud), ensure the A record is set to **DNS only** (gray cloud) during initial SSL provisioning. You can re-enable proxying after the certificate is issued.
</Warning>

---

## What the Emergent subdomain is

Every web app on Emergent is assigned a default URL in the format:

```
https://yourappname.emergent.build
```

This subdomain:

- Is **always available**, even if you add a custom domain.
- Receives the same deployments and updates as your custom domain.
- Uses a **wildcard SSL certificate** managed by Emergent (always HTTPS).
- Reflects the **app name** you chose during creation.

<Callout type="info" title="Will the subdomain work as-is?">
Yes. You can share the `yourappname.emergent.build` URL immediately — no DNS setup required. It is a fully functional production URL. Custom domains are optional and purely for branding.
</Callout>

If you are prototyping or running an internal tool, the Emergent subdomain is often sufficient. For customer-facing apps, a custom domain (e.g., `app.yourcompany.com`) is recommended.

---

## Changing the app name & Google auth label

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="Can I rename my app (and subdomain)?">
Yes. In the workspace **Settings** → **App Name**, you can rename your app. The Emergent subdomain will update to `newappname.emergent.build`. Existing links using the old subdomain will break, so update any bookmarks or shared URLs.

<Warning>
Renaming the app does **not** automatically update OAuth redirect URIs in third-party providers (Google, GitHub, etc.). If you use [Google auth](/google-auth) or [Emergent Auth](/emergent-auth-built-in), you must also update the authorized redirect URI in the Google Cloud Console or GitHub OAuth app settings to match the new subdomain.
</Warning>
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Why does Google auth show 'Sign in to [old app name]'?">
Google's OAuth consent screen displays the **OAuth application name** configured in the Google Cloud Console, not the Emergent app name. To change the label users see:

1. Go to the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com).
2. Select your project → **APIs & Services** → **OAuth consent screen**.
3. Update the **Application name** field.
4. Save changes.

The new name will appear on the Google sign-in prompt within a few minutes. For more details, see the [Google auth](/google-auth) page.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
